positions.title: The rook must change checking ranks
positions.sourceLabel: P99 · Checking distance and rank changes
positions.prompt: Rh8+ forces the king to d7, but the follow-up must check from the seventh rank rather than offering the rook on d8. Trace the defender's reply exactly; compare the second legal plan rather than assuming a forced win.

positions.continuationReason: Rh7+ reaches the new rank while preserving distance from the opposing king.
positions.explanation: The rook must change checking ranks. Rh8+ forces the king to d7, but the follow-up must check from the seventh rank rather than offering the rook on d8. Main illustrative line: h1h8 e8d7 h8h7. Counterline: h1h6 a8a7 h6h7. ...Kd7 is an actual king flight; Black's rook on a8 also makes a rook trade on the eighth rank dangerous. Endpoint: Rh7+ reaches the new rank while preserving distance from the opposing king. Repair this misunderstanding: Shifting to d8 after ...Kd7 would leave White's rook exposed to ...Rxd8; forcing checks require tactical safety. This is not a tablebase-certified winning line or proof of unique best play. Technique study: Checking distance is a defensive and offensive resource: a rook far from the king can give repeated checks without immediate capture. If the defending king leaves the eighth rank, the attacker must reconstruct checking lanes on the seventh or sixth; rook moves to squares attacked by the opponent's rook may lose material. Always name the defended rook's square and the king's next legal flight.
